photos.selftext: We’re sharing a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, one of the deepest problems at the frontier of mathematics. The proof was produced by a group of agents, using an OpenAI next-generation model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra. The problem concerns whether the description of smooth three-dimensional fluid motion modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations can break down. It has remained unresolved for roughly 90 years.

photos.selftext: Hi. 😊 Swedish dude here. When our children get sick, we have 60 paid days per year to stay home with them. Per parent. They're separate from my 25 paid vacation days. Meaning I don't have to use my own paid sick leave. If I'm a single parent: 120 days. If my child has a chronic illness: 120 days If my child is hospitalized: unlimited days. These days reset every January. By law. every year until child is 18. Follow for more glimpses into life in a social democracy, where dignity is not a privilege.￼ Peace ✌🏼

photos.selftext: It seems most people don't understand how severe the energy situation is right now in the Middle East. As of Friday, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has officially been shut down after recent attacks, putting -4 million barrels of daily oil exports at risk. Meanwhile, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait is now at risk of being shut down, threatening up to -9 million barrels of daily oil supply. All while the Strait of Hormuz is operating at ~20% of its pre-Iran War capacity, removing -15 million barrels of daily oil flows. Combined, this represents nearly ~30 MILLION barrels per day of oil flows that are either offline or at risk. Even after accounting for some overlap between these routes, the scale of the potential disruption is enormous relative to the ~100 million barrel per day global oil market. This is one of the most severe energy supply situations in modern history.

photos.selftext: In 2001, actor Mark Ruffalo woke up in the middle of the night from a dream that he had a brain tumor. He had no symptoms at all. But the dream disturbed him enough to ask the doctor on his film set to check. The next day, a scan showed a tumor the size of a golf ball behind his left ear. The tumor was benign, but it was pressing on a facial nerve and had to be removed. Doctors warned him the surgery could leave him deaf, paralyzed on one side of his face, or both. There was one more problem. His wife was about to give birth to their first child. So Mark said nothing. He kept the diagnosis from his wife until a week after their son was born. When he finally told her, she thought he was joking. A few weeks later, surgeons removed the tumor. He woke up with the left side of his face frozen and no hearing in his left ear. His face took almost a year to recover. His hearing never did. Mark Ruffalo has been deaf in his left ear ever since.
